scope: Parent evidence about the running Engram process and about what a graceful stop does to WAL sidecars. The checkpoint test ran on a private cp -a copy of ~/.engram, never on the real directory.

running_process.supervision: not a systemd unit; lives in transient scope app-Hyprland-xdg\x2dterminal\x2dexec-6edb38c6.scope created by xdg-terminal-exec, so it was launched from a terminal session
running_process.implication: The HTTP API on port 7437 serves the shared store to whatever other tooling uses it; nothing about this process is specific to isSWF.

before.compatibility: exit 2, unsafe or invalid fixture metadata

conclusions: The store is healthy: integrity_check ok and 28 tables on a faithful copy.
The 27 MB WAL folds into engram.db when the last connection closes cleanly, and SQLite then removes -wal and -shm.
The preflight rejection is a side effect of sidecar files existing on disk, not a defect in the data.
Observed on the real store: a graceful stop of engram serve leaves the sidecars in place, so the rejection is not limited to a live store.

stop.sidecars_after_stop: engram.db-wal (27896552 B, mtime unchanged) and engram.db-shm (32768 B, mtime updated) still present
stop.engram.db_mtime: updated to stop time, size unchanged

restart.command: cd /home/iseoane/Work/agent-depot && ENGRAM_CLOUD_AUTOSYNC=1 setsid nohup engram serve

stop_restart_on_real_store.autosync_on_restart: [autosync] ERROR: cloud token is not configured ... autosync disabled; GET /sync/status reports enabled=false, reason blocked_unenrolled
stop_restart_on_real_store.correction: The copy-based prediction that a graceful stop clears the sidecars did NOT hold on the real store. internal/store/compatibility.go L60 therefore keeps rejecting this directory whether or not the store is open, so `compatibility` cannot serve as its preflight. The same file name rule also means the rejection is permanent for any store Engram has opened in WAL mode and left with sidecars.

push_versus_sidecars: These are unrelated mechanisms and the earlier report mixed them. -wal/-shm exist because a process has the store open in WAL mode, and engram's own shutdown does not remove them. sync.log records the user's git chunk export/import hooks per project (Import OK, Pull OK, Push OK, Chunks nuevos commiteados), not cloud traffic; cloud has no server URL or token and autosync disables itself. Its 121 'binario engram no encontrado en el PATH del hook' warnings and 3 real rebase conflicts are that mechanism's own backlog, unrelated to isSWF.
relevance_to_isSWF: None of the observed projects or the push concern isSWF. Two consequences for integration: pass an explicit --project (the running serve process has cwd ~/Work/agent-depot, so cwd detection would attribute calls to it), and treat the shared store as hosting other projects whose content must never be read into our context.
real_store_effect: None. Only a read-only copy was opened; ~/.engram kept identical sizes and mtimes for db, sidecars, identity and locks.
limits: The copy was taken while the store was open, so it is not an atomic snapshot and says nothing about writes that had not reached the WAL. No memory contents were inspected. The stop/restart was performed with operator awareness; the relaunched process runs detached from a shell instead of its original terminal scope.
